svg.text: The bunching below the threshold is broad, and no matching hole opens above it
Figure 12's excess-mass estimator, imported and pointed at one department or product family at a time, then mirrored to read the two bins just above the line.
an auditor deciding where to point a below-threshold screen, and
whether a below-line award is a moved one
whether to target a buyer, a product family or a vehicle, and
whether to read the excess as work held under the line
a ring sits left of the null band -- a real hole above the line
-- or the filled marks collapse into it
filled: awards in the two $5,000 bins just below the line, against the local trend
ring: the two bins just above it
band: middle 80% of the same subgroups read at $200,000 and $300,000, where no rule exists
14 of 27 subgroups exceed the band below the line; 1 falls under it above, where chance alone gives 3
BY PRODUCT OR SERVICE FAMILY, 16 OF 33 SCORED
largest holds 162 awards, the floor is 400
12 of 20 subgroups exceed the band below the line; 1 falls under it above, where chance alone gives 2
BY PRODUCT OR SERVICE FAMILY, 11 OF 33 SCORED
largest holds 132 awards, the floor is 400
USAspending API v2 bulk download, fetched 2026-09-22; FY2017 and FY2025, positive awards only, using figure 12's estimator unchanged. CAVEAT: the deficit above the line is no deeper at
the rule than at values with no rule behind it, so nothing here shows the excess is work moved down rather than work that was always small. These eleven civilian departments are 8.5% of
federal contract awards; Defense (68.6%) is absent, so this is not federal procurement as a whole.
